html:
The Palace of Blachernae was an imperial residence in the northwest corner of Constantinople, where the land walls meet the Golden Horn. From the reign of Alexios I Komnenos it replaced the old Great Palace near Hagia Sophia as the emperors' main home.

There had been a palace here, beside a famous church of the Virgin, since about 500. The Komnenos emperors rebuilt and enlarged it, and Manuel I added a grand new hall. Western visitors were dazzled by its gold, marble and mosaics. Close to the walls, it was also easier to defend and to leave from than the old palace by the sea.

In 1203 the knights of the Fourth Crusade attacked the walls nearby in the siege of 1203, and the Latin emperors later lived here. After the city was retaken in 1261, the Palaiologos emperors made it their home again. It was run down by the Ottoman conquest of 1453. Little survives apart from the Tekfur Palace, which may have been part of the complex.
